basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 1.' and it opens 'Vers. 1. Adduxit spiritum. Id est ventum, vel, ut quidam volunt, solem, sive Spiritum'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 1. Adduxit spiritum. Id est ventum, vel, ut quidam volunt, solem, sive Spiritum sanctum debemus accipere de quo in principio dicitur: Spiritus Domini ferebatur super aquas. Qui enim in principio ferebatur super aquas, ut eas in unum congregaret, ut appareret arida, ipse nunc sua et totius Trinitatis voluntate adductus est super terram, ut a pervasione aquarum eriperet eam, et eis pristinam pulchritudinem | et fertilitatem redderet.
